Yes — your USB-C cable can limit charging speed. The cable, charger, and device all need to support the required power level for you to get the fastest possible charge. A 240W cable won't force your device to charge at 240W; it simply supports a higher maximum power level.

60W vs. 100W vs. 240W
60W

20V × 3A

Best for phones, tablets, and many laptops

Suitable for devices that need up to 60W. A 60W cable may limit a laptop that needs more power, potentially slowing charging during heavy use.

100W

20V × 5A

Best for many USB-C laptops

Supports up to 100W with a compatible charger and device. The cable in the provided results is a 100W, 5A, e-marked cable. It is not rated for 140W or 240W charging.

240W

48V × 5A

Best for high-power laptops and future-proofing

Supports USB Power Delivery Extended Power Range (EPR), including compatible 140W, 180W, and 240W setups. These cables require an e-marker.

One important detail: USB-IF and UL Solutions describe compliant USB-C-to-USB-C cables under the newer specification as 60W or 240W categories. A cable advertised as 100W may refer to an older rating or a manufacturer's product specification, so check the actual cable's compliance and capabilities.

How to know which cable you need

Your charger is 30–60W: A suitable 60W cable is generally enough.

Your charger is 65–100W: Choose a cable rated for the power your device needs; the Baseus cable above is one option.

Your laptop needs 140W or more: Choose a compatible 240W EPR cable and charger.

Your device charges slowly despite a powerful charger: Check the cable rating, charger compatibility, and your device's maximum supported charging power.

USB-IF also provides a certified product search where you can check whether a product is listed as certified.

Bottom line: For most everyday charging, 60W is enough. For many laptops, 100W is a useful target. For devices that support charging above 100W, choose a 240W EPR cable.
